title: Back to Nursery — Settling & Transitions
strapline: New room, new faces, new starts — settling in, gently and together.
intent: Times of transition — starting nursery, moving rooms, coming back after a break — need warmth, routine and reassurance.
Talking through feelings about change helps children name worry, excitement and everything in between.
Familiar faces, comfort objects and predictable rhythms give children a secure base to explore from.
Getting to know new friends and grown-ups grows belonging, confidence and social connection.
The theme supports every child to feel safe, known and ready to settle and play.
implementation: Keep transition times gentle and predictable — familiar routines, a key person close, comfort objects welcome.
Talk openly about feelings: 'It can feel funny starting somewhere new — lots of us feel a bit wobbly at first.'
Make the new room and faces familiar — photos of grown-ups and friends, a settling-in book, a tour of where things are.
Welcome a comfort object or family photo from home as a bridge to security.
Build belonging with getting-to-know-you games, name songs and a spot that is each child's own.
Follow each child's pace — some settle in a morning, others need a familiar adult close for weeks.
key_questions: How are you feeling about being here today?
What would help you feel comfy and safe?
Who are the grown-ups who look after you here?
Shall we find your peg and your special spot?
What do you like doing best when you're here?

impact.text: Children settle with support from a familiar adult and use them as a safe base.
Children name and talk about their feelings about change.
Children get to know new friends and grown-ups and grow in belonging.
Children follow the room's routines and rhythms with reminders.
Children grow in confidence to try new things and join in.

enhancements: A settling-in book with photos of grown-ups, friends and the room.
A welcome spot for each child — a peg, a tray, a photo — that is theirs.
A comfort-object and family-photo policy so home comes with them.
Getting-to-know-you name songs and games for the group.
A feelings board or puppets for talking about big changes.

playing_exploring: Children explore the room and new play at their own pace as they settle.
They begin to feel safe enough to have a go at new things.
active_learning: Children draw on a familiar adult and grow steadily in independence.
They keep coming back to try again as confidence builds.
creating_thinking: Children make sense of the change and what helps them feel safe.
They connect new faces and places to their growing sense of belonging.
